prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm O&M; scope: offshore assets, marine/shore facilities, personnel, external orgs, electrical up to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere: farm/transmission boundary, holds dispatch boundary while local systems run turbines, exchanges authorized signals, normal-supply/protection status); excludes public grid, non-farm port ops. Turbine Controller (Glassfin): executes authorized control, limits output, blocks protection-conflicting commands, reports state, safe mode on auxiliary loss; produces Pitch Deviation Notice. Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet (interlocks), Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus. Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur): imagery. Offshore Substation (Morrowick): Main Transformer, export cable, Export Cable Monitor, station service transformers (essential/nonessential separated). Emergency Generator (Foxglove): auto-starts on auxiliary loss, transfers within V/f limits, no unapproved paralleling/export, sheds nonessential on overload, failure→alarm keeping UPS; transfers back when stable. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale): status/alarms/relay data to Shore Control Room (Amber Quay: coordinates notices/interface decisions, overview of marine ops/restrictions); flags work from Pitch Deviation Notice; produces Session Revocation Receipt. Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown): ranks work by condition, safety, production, access, resources; standby-electrical reviews; uses Squall Window Bulletin. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard): allocates output within limits; uses Position Quality Flag for movement planning. Grid Dispatcher sets dispatch. Frequency response only if authorized; comms loss keeps protection; Grid Constraint→reduce/redispatch/disconnect; alarms safety>protection>export; normal export resumes only when interface stable and protections available. Marine: Marine Coordinator (daily plan, resolves conflicts, records/distributes changes), Duty Planner (reprioritizes; Transfer Manifest Addendum), Vessel Master (departure readiness), Crew Transfer Vessel (Kestrel Bay, within limits), SOV (extended support), Daughter Craft (only after review), Helideck, Port Agent, Rescue Coordinator, Operations Radio Console. Weather Service forecasts; Weather Analyst advises Marine Coordinator; Metocean Buoy (Copper Finch): sea conditions, Wave Burst Record; Weather Hold when limits unsafe. Vessel AIS Receiver (Blue Granite): Position Quality Flag. Personnel Tracking Console (roster, return times), North/South Access Scanners. HSE Officer produces Harness Audit Card pre-transfer. Warehouse System (Mosslight):

New part:
S247: The Duty Planner reviews the ranked queue and confirms that urgent work has a clear technical basis and a feasible execution path.
S248: Confirmed faults that threaten personnel safety or cause substantial generation loss receive priority over routine inspections.
S249: Planned work is advanced when its due date, condition evidence, and operational value justify the required outage or vessel time.
S250: The Nacelle Condition Monitor provides condition data that helps distinguish developing degradation from transient alarms.
S251: The Turbine Sensor Bus provides operating measurements for work that depends on recent machine behavior.
S252: The Export Cable Monitor helps planners assess whether cable condition warrants inspection or corrective intervention.
S253: The Field Supervisor checks reported faults against available evidence and identifies work that requires an offshore visit.
S254: The Blade Inspection Drone can support inspection planning when blade access from a vessel or by rope team is not justified.
S255: The Weather Service supplies forecast information for evaluating marine and aviation access options.
S256: The Weather Analyst reviews forecast confidence and highlights conditions that could invalidate a planned access period.
S257: The Marine Coordinator compares expected access conditions with vessel capability, transit time, and worksite limits.
S258: The Duty Planner considers Crew Transfer Vessel, Daughter Craft, Service Operations Vessel, and Helideck access when selecting a mobilization method.
S259: A Weather Hold prevents mobilization when forecast or observed conditions exceed the approved operating limits.
S260: Sable Orchard assigns vessel and crew resources to approved work packages after the Duty Planner confirms the operating priority.
S261: The Marine Coordinator coordinates resource changes with the Vessel Master and affected work teams.
S262: The Storekeeper uses the exception slip to validate an unavailable part before the work package is rescheduled.
S263: The Duty Planner accounts for part availability, technician competence, and estimated task duration before committing a work window.
S264: Work packages with long lead requirements are scheduled early enough to avoid avoidable vessel standby and repeat mobilization.
S265: The Work Permit Portal supports readiness checks for work requiring controlled access or electrical isolation.
S266: The HSE Officer reviews hazards and confirms that proposed controls match the task scope and site conditions.
S267: The Offshore Substation sends a Transformer Tap Snapshot when a transformer condition review is requested.
S268: The Substation Operator confirms local operating constraints before substation work is placed in the executable plan.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
